route: implied_parameter_monotonicity
evidence: Each Kirby MCQ item text states its own immediate/delayed amounts and delay, so it implies a discount rate k=(LDR-SIR)/(SIR*delay). Parsed k from our item_text for all 27 items and correlated it with the live proportion choosing the delayed option (resp=2): Spearman rho=+0.961, Pearson on log k =+0.961, in the correct direction, with the extremes exactly as theory requires (k=0.00016 items: 4-7% choose delayed; k=0.25 items: 97%). Items sharing a k differ only by reward magnitude, the expected magnitude effect. A permuted item_text mapping would destroy this relationship, so this is a strong item-by-item verification. Also confirms the codes follow canonical Kirby ordering (mc1 = $54 vs $55/117d).

route: route 6 (keying polarity) + route 8 (semantic coherence of item means), used to adjudicate variable-label vs column-name (issue #1654)
evidence: Name-vs-label conflict resolved in favour of the labels, decisively. (1) Coherence: the 10 labels, read in column order, reproduce the RSES in the standard circulated administration order (canonical Rosenberg-1965 items 7,3,9,4,5,10,1,8,6,2), i.e. a known permutation, not a scramble; the column names follow the Rosenberg-1965 order 1..10. Names and labels agree only on dowell304, noproud305, morerespect308. (2) Keying polarity on the raw, unreversed data (N=374 complete cases): the correlation matrix splits into a positive block {301,302,304,306,307,308} and a negative block {303,305,309,310} (e.g. r(302,304)=+0.39, r(302,307)=+0.39, r(303,309)=+0.26, r(309,310)=+0.30, r(302,310)=-0.19, r(303,304)=-0.28). The two hypotheses differ on exactly four columns, and the data agree with the LABEL hypothesis on all four: 302 positive (label 'number of good qualities'; the name nogood302 would predict negative), 303 negative (label 'I am a failure'; name goodqualities303 would predict positive), 306 positive (label 'positive attitude'; name usefull306 would predict negative), 310 negative (label 'no good at all'; name positiveattitude310 would predict positive). (3) Means corroborate: 303=1.47 and 309=1.55 (near-floor, correct for 'failure'/'useless') while 302=3.28 and 306=3.19 (near-ceiling, correct for 'good qualities'/'positive attitude') -- the reverse of what the column names imply. morerespect308 sits with the positive block (r=+0.20..+0.33) despite negative wording, the well-documented behaviour of that RSES item in this very sample (the paper drops it, alpha .61 -> .72, citing Schmitt & Allik's Ethiopian alpha of .33); both hypotheses assign it the same text, so it is not diagnostic either way. (4) Anchor direction cross-checked against the sibling PSS-10 in the same .sav (0 Never..4 Very Often, unambiguous): under the .sav's RSES value labels (1 Strongly Disagree..4 Strongly Agree, as used by the processing script) the positive-worded RSES block correlates -0.28 with the distress-worded PSS items and +0.39 with the coping-worded ones, and the negative block flips both signs (+0.40 / -0.24) -- the expected pattern. The paper's Methods sentence '1 (strongly agree) to 4 (strongly disagree)' is therefore wrong for the archived data and was not followed.

route: route 6 (keying polarity) + route 7 (marker item)
evidence: Neither the .xlsx (headers S1..S10, 'Data dictionary' sheet scale-level only) nor the paper ties any code to an item, so the order was reconstructed and tested. Route 5 (subscale blocks, server-side CORR self-join, n=519): 13/13 items have their weakest within-block r above their strongest cross-block r; within-block mean r +0.750 (min +0.615) vs cross-block mean +0.144 (max +0.594), so the test is powered, not a general-factor artifact. This confirms the S3 Appendix's four headed blocks ME(4)/VE(3)/SP(3)/PES(3) map onto the ME/VE/SP/PES column prefixes. Route 6 (polarity): the 3 negatively worded PES items correlate -0.137/-0.191/-0.216 with the 10 positively worded items while all 10 of those correlate +0.420..+0.571 with each other, so PES is stored RAW and the shipped negative wording matches the data direction. Corroboration: CFA-phase (cov_study='cfa', N=295) per-item mean range 3.722-5.871 and SD range 1.042-1.500 reproduce the paper's stated 3.72-5.87 and 1.04-1.50 exactly. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: the S3 Appendix numbers items 1..13 CONTINUOUSLY under subscale headings and never prints the code strings ME1/ME2/..., so the numeric suffix is inferred from print order within a block -- this is a block-level label match, not a code-level one, and the standing 'explicit code labels in the paper' exemption does not reach the suffix. Nothing here distinguishes ME1 from ME2 or SP1/SP2/SP3; 4!*3!*3!*3! = 5184 within-block orderings survive every number above. Rival routes tried and failed: the paper's Tables 4/5 give loadings/alpha/CR/AVE per FACTOR only, never per item (route 1 unavailable); cross-instrument content matching on the deposit's Study3 sheet (n=304 who answered both scales) is swamped by a general factor (ME2 vs its content twin LSE5 r=.530 but ME2 vs PSE2 r=.591), so it does not recover within-block order.

route: explicit subscale-code labels in S2 Appendix + code-is-source-column-name derivation + live-vs-deposit per-item aggregate identity + paper Fig 2 per-item CFA loading reproduction (route 1-style); cross-instrument content correlations (route 8) attempted and underpowered
evidence: Code derivation: data/wang_2024_speaking_self_efficacy.py selects the S1 Data columns BY NAME (LSE1..PSE4) and melts with var_name='item' -- the live item code IS the source column header, no rename and no positional assignment (core model s3 row 1). Live-vs-deposit: a server-side GROUP BY aggregate on the live table (redivis query, no export) reproduces every deposit column exactly for all 15/15 items over the pooled 227 efa + 289 cfa = 516 respondents -- mean/sd to <0.005 (LSE1 4.00/1.23, LSE3 3.41/1.17, DSE2 3.53/1.30, PSE4 4.39/1.36), max, and the integer count of resp=7 (LSE1 7, LSE2 9, LSE3 0, LSE4 1, LSE5 6, SRE1 17, SRE2 28, SRE3 31, DSE1 11, DSE2 10, DSE3 24, PSE1 16, PSE2 13, PSE3 10, PSE4 32); LSE3 is the only item never rated 7 (max 6) in both, and the SRE2/SRE3 mean tie at 4.94 is broken by sd 1.23 vs 1.18 and n7 28 vs 31. Authors' own labels: paper Fig 2 prints per-item standardized CFA loadings against these codes (N=289, deposit sheet Study1-cfa); refitting the 4-factor correlated model reproduces all 15 to <=0.005 (LSE1 .842 vs .84, LSE3 .705 vs .70, DSE1 .903 vs .90, PSE2 .908 vs .91, PSE4 .733 vs .73), and 13 of 15 are distinct within their own block (LSE4 and LSE5 both .81). Text side: S2 Appendix prints the 15 items numbered 1-15 CONTINUOUSLY under four subscale headers -- 'Linguistic Self-Efficacy (LSE)' items 1-5, 'Self-Regulatory Efficacy (SRE)' 6-8, 'Delivery Self-efficacy (DSE)' 9-11, 'Performance Self-Efficacy (PSE)' 12-15; block sizes 5/3/3/4 match the deposit's column counts and the paper's Table 1. The string 'LSE' occurs EXACTLY ONCE in the appendix's document.xml, in that header: no per-item code is printed anywhere in the file. So the standing 'explicit code labels in the paper' exemption holds for the SUBSCALE PREFIX only -- the numeric suffix is the item's position inside its labelled block, i.e. a positional inference. Attempted and underpowered: cross-instrument content pairing on the deposit's Study3 sheet (N=304, same respondents took both scales) -- ME2 ('correct pronunciation, intonation, and liaison') should peak on the identically worded LSE5 but the LSE-block max is LSE1 r=0.564 vs LSE5 r=0.530, and ME4 ('excellent grades on Spoken English tests') should peak on PSE4 but the PSE-block max is PSE3 r=0.693 while PSE4 is the block MINIMUM r=0.499; a general factor dominates all 195 cross-scale correlations, so this is a failure of the test rather than evidence against the mapping. NOT ESTABLISHED: the within-block ordering. Nothing here distinguishes LSE1 from LSE2 (or the order within SRE, DSE, PSE); rotating the five LSE texts among LSE1..LSE5 would leave every number above unchanged. What IS established: every item's subscale membership, by the appendix's own block labels, and the identity of the live code with the deposit column the paper itself labels. CAVEAT ON PROVENANCE: the shipped provenance note claims the appendix uses 'the same LSE/SRE/DSE/PSE codes the response columns use, so no positional inference'; that is true of the prefix and false of the suffix. No sign that anything shipped is wrong -- the appendix's print order and the deposit's column order agree block for block -- but the mapping is corroborated, not label-matched, at item level.

route: 6 (keying polarity) + 3 (published subgroup totals) + published alpha & deposit banner for block boundary
evidence: Code derivation is POSITIONAL inside a labelled block, not a label match: the deposit's columns are Q8_1..Q8_19 and the AP1..AP19 codes appear nowhere in the data, so data/xue_2025_academic_procrastination.py's Q8_<i>->AP<i> rename is an order inference. Step 5b's 'explicit code labels in the paper' exemption therefore does NOT apply, contrary to the provenance note's claim that the mapping is 'explicit rather than order-inferred'. BLOCK BOUNDARY (settled, 3 independent ways): S1 Data's banner row labels col 9 'Academic Procrastination', col 28 'Academic Stress', col 48 'Negative coping style', giving blocks of exactly 19/20/20 columns against S3 File's 19 AP / 20 AS / 20 CSS stems; Cronbach's alpha over the 19 shipped items AS STORED is 0.871 against the paper's Table 2 value of 0.871 (reverse-scoring the 4 pro-study items would give 0.914, so the data are raw); and Table 3's academic-procrastination row reproduces EXACTLY from the sum of these 19 items -- high-stress group 63.864 SD 11.140 (n=147, AS total > 73rd pctile) vs published 63.864 SD 11.140, low-stress group 51.387 SD 11.248 (n=173, AS total <= 27th pctile) vs published 51.387 SD 11.248. No off-by-one or cross-construct block error. ITEM-LEVEL (route 6, keying polarity): S3 File's AP block contains exactly 4 pro-study stems (AP8 'organize my study materials', AP13 'detailed plan for preparing for exams', AP18 'a study plan every day', AP19 'check the tasks I should complete before entertainment'); in the live data the corrected item-total r is +0.007 / -0.169 / -0.206 / -0.092 for exactly those four and +0.457 to +0.730 for the other 15 -- a 4/4 hit classifying 19/19 positions, p = 1/C(19,4) = 0.00026 under a random permutation. All 19 live per-item means also reproduce the deposit's Q8_i column means to 2dp (AP1 2.75, AP7 3.53, AP8 3.66, AP15 2.63, ...). NOT ESTABLISHED: within-class order. Checks on alpha and Table 3 totals are order-invariant and pin only the block; polarity separates the 4 pro-study items from the 15 procrastination items but distinguishes neither the 15 from each other nor the 4 from each other, so a permutation confined within a class (AP2<->AP5, AP13<->AP18) would pass. The paper publishes no per-item statistics (Tables 1-9 are scale-level), all 19 items share one 1-5 scale so there is no range fingerprint, and Zhao (2007)'s subscale structure is not reported, so no route closes that gap. PARTIAL, not VERIFIED. Re-runnable as verify_xue_2025_academic_procrastination.R (VERDICT: PASS).

route: block boundary (source banner + published alpha/KMO) + route 7 marker item + route 8 semantic coherence; routes 1,2,5,6,9 unavailable
evidence: Code derivation is NOT a label match: S3 File labels items (AS1)-(AS20), but the S1 Data spreadsheet's columns are Q9_1-Q9_20 and carry no item text, so data/xue_2025_academic_procrastination.py's rename Q9_i -> AS_i is an ORDER inference, not the paper's own label. The Step 5b 'explicit code labels in the paper' exemption therefore does NOT apply and the provenance note's claim that the mapping is 'explicit rather than order-inferred' is overstated. BLOCK BOUNDARY (settled): S1 Data banner row 0 labels col 8 'Academic Procrastination' (Q8_1), col 27 'Academic Stress' (Q9_1), col 47 'Negative coping style' (Q10_1); S3 File lists AP1-AP19, then AS1-AS20 contiguously, then CSS1-CSS20; live AS1-AS20 reproduce source Q9_1-Q9_20 exactly (n=579 each, mean/sd to 4 dp, e.g. AS1 3.5561/0.9851, AS20 2.1641/1.1234). Alpha over live AS1-AS20 = 0.9169 and KMO = 0.9324 vs the paper's published 0.917 / 0.932; the off-by-one window Q8_19..Q9_19 gives alpha 0.9134 and Q9_2..Q10_1 gives 0.9105, neither rounding to 0.917. So no cross-construct (AP/CSS) contamination and no boundary shift. WITHIN-BLOCK ORDER (route 7 marker + route 8 semantics): AS20 (romantic relationships, the only non-academic stem) is uniquely the least endorsed item, mean 2.16, 37.0% at floor, lowest mean inter-item r 0.172 and lowest item-total 0.28; the highest correlations pair semantic twins - AS2/AS6 employability r=0.685, AS4/AS5 exam+workload 0.642, AS13/AS16 school-environment 0.612, AS9/AS10 self-expectation vs future 0.594. Over all 20 cyclic realignments of text to column, the shipped identity alignment uniquely maximises the mean of those five a-priori twin-pair correlations (0.602 vs next-best 0.463) and is the only one placing the romance stem on the least-endorsed column. ROUTES THAT FAILED OR DID NOT APPLY: route 1 - the paper publishes no per-item M/SD, no floor/ceiling and no factor loadings, only scale-level alpha/KMO, which are permutation-invariant and carry no order information. Route 2 - all 20 items share one 1-5 scale, no range signature. Route 5 - the paper names four dimensions (personal, familial, institutional, social) but publishes NO item-to-dimension assignment, so a content-derived grouping had to be used; it scored 6/20, which is uninformative rather than adverse: alpha 0.917 with mean inter-item r 0.360 means the scale is dominated by a general factor and the block test is underpowered here (the alsuhibani_2022_gcbs case). Route 6 - no reverse-worded stems in this instrument and no negative item-total in the data (min 0.28, AS20), so there is no polarity signal to read. Route 9 - the source stores integers, not labels; nothing to match. NOT ESTABLISHED: the routes rule out cross-construct contamination, a block-boundary shift and any cyclic realignment, and pin AS20 individually. They do NOT distinguish local transpositions of semantically similar neighbours - AS4 vs AS5 (both exam/workload, r=0.642, means 3.62 vs 3.42), AS13 vs AS16 (both school environment, r=0.612), AS3 vs AS19 (both parental expectation), AS2 vs AS6 (both employability). Settling those needs the Chinese instrument (Liu 2015), which is not recoverable from the article or its supplements. Hence PARTIAL, not VERIFIED. Item wording itself was re-diffed against S3 File: all 20 stems match verbatim, including the AS7 source typo.

A permutation test over all 720 orderings, scoring both columns on their own error scales, ranks the shipped order DT1..DT6 first of 720 (3.69) with the next-best ordering -- the DT3/DT4 swap -- at 5.70, so every item is distinguished from every other. The DT3/DT4 pair is the thinnest link and is separated by the loading column, not the VIF column: their published VIFs differ by only 0.001 and a swap costs just 7e-4 in VIF, while in loadings the shipped residuals are -0.000/+0.002 against -0.010/+0.012 if swapped. Route 1: refitting the paper's own one-factor SIB CFA on the four items Table 2 retained reproduces the published standardized loadings and R-SQUARE on n=336 -- published 0.707/0.500, 0.903/0.815, 0.775/0.601, 0.754/0.569 for SIB1, SIB2, SIB3, SIB6 vs observed 0.7072/0.5002, 0.9026/0.8147, 0.7752/0.6010, 0.7544/0.5691, largest deviation 0.0004; Table 2 is an image, so those numbers are in no machine-readable form. A sweep of all 360 ordered 4-of-6 assignments puts the shipped one uniquely first (SSD 0.000000 vs 0.000878 for the runner-up SIB1,SIB2,SIB6,SIB3). Route 8: the article attributes the two SIB deletions to residuals that 'were not independent and were strongly correlated', and the pair missing from Table 2 is {SIB4,SIB5} -- the sentences shipped for those two codes are the block's only implementation pair, and SIB4-SIB5 is the tightest pair in the data on both measures (raw r = 0.738, the largest of the 15 pairs; one-factor residual correlation 0.120 against 0.073 for the next largest). PARTIAL, not VERIFIED: these pin the live columns to the paper's codes and corroborate the text-to-code tie for the excluded pair, but nothing in the data says which implementation sentence is SIB4 and which is SIB5, nor which sentence goes with SIB1 vs SIB3 (item means span only 4.77-5.23 and no content prediction separates them) -- both rest on the S1 Appendix's own 1-6 numbering.

route: 3 (published subscale total, alpha and Table 2 correlation) + elimination against the ERQ's canonical suppression numbering
evidence: Route 3 (published subscale statistics), computed from the deposit .xlsx and re-runnable as verify_li_2024_bdyz.R: raw sum of BDYZ1/2/6/9 gives mean 14.66 / SD 5.61 / N 1,151 against the paper's published Expressive Suppression total of 14.66 / 5.61 / 1,151; Cronbach's alpha 0.8336 vs published 0.834; r(ES, reverse-scored SPA total) = 0.219 vs the 0.219 printed in Table 2, with the SPA total itself checked at 43.21 / 10.52 vs published 43.21 / 10.52. That fixes the block identity (this is the ES subscale, not the 'body-image scale' of the dictionary Description) and the coding direction (raw, unreversed; a reversed reading would give 17.34). Item-level: the paper ties 'item 9' to "I don't express sadness and anger when I feel it", which is ERQ item 9, so bdyz_9 is pinned; bdyz_2 and bdyz_6 follow the ERQ's own suppression numbering (2, 6) but nothing in the data separates them from each other; bdyz_1 is assigned ERQ item 4 by elimination, its corrected item-total of 0.628 (vs 0.652 / 0.695 / 0.678) ruling out ERQ item 1, a reappraisal item, but not identifying item 4 positively. So the route does NOT distinguish every item from every other item -- three of the four assignments rest on the deposit's numbering plus elimination, not on a stated correspondence.
